findings.text: _attempt_deadline_seconds has two branches: the deadline a manifest quotes back via _FENCE_STATEMENT, and the attempt.json+node.time_budget fallback. Only the fallback branch is exercised by tests/test_time_fence_follows_the_attempt.py (the fixture writes attempt.json and never a quoted fence). A regression in the quoted-statement regex or its parse would leave the check silently inert for manifests that quote their fence, and no test would catch it. Add a case whose manifest text carries 'Launched <iso> UTC; deadline <iso>' and assert the deadline is read from it.

The base arm ran from a git-archive extraction under $TMPDIR that is not a git worktree, and about ten tests/test_gate_evidence.py cases fail there because the promote path resolves a git root from the working directory ('Error: run ... is classified promotable; no complete independent review is stored'), not because of the code under test. I reproduced this: the same base reports.py passes tests/test_gate_evidence.py::test_armed_promotion_refuses_missing_observation_and_keeps_pointer when the working directory is inside a git repo, and fails when it is inside the archive. So the recorded base failure set (14) is inflated by ~10 spurious ids and the 14-vs-3 comparison reads as the change fixing eleven tests. added_failure_count is still 0 because every head failure id is also a base id. The remedy is to run the base arm from a git checkout (or git-init the extraction before the gate) so its failure set is meaningful.
